mem.t: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

lessons.title: The Rest of the Seventh Day
lessons.theme: Rest is a gift God built into creation

v: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
“Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

lessons.still: Put down whatever is in your hands. Sit back in your chair and let your shoulders drop. Tell the Lord, “Lord, you rested from your work on the seventh day; today I too will rest a while before you.” Quietly enjoy the freedom of this moment, when there is nothing you have to do.
teach: A musical score has rests in it. They are not mistakes but part of the music; a piece with no rests would be nothing but noise. In the rhythm of creation, God also wrote in a rest: the seventh day.

God rested from his work not because he was tired, but because the work was finished and he wanted to enjoy the goodness of what he had made. He “blessed the seventh day, and made it holy”—the first thing in the Bible that God set apart as holy was not a place but a span of time. The Ten Commandments also say, “Remember the Sabbath day,” reminding us that we are not machines but living beings made in God’s image, who need rhythm.

People today see rest as a waste and busyness as a mark of worth. Our mindset needs to change: rest is not a reward for work but God’s command and God’s gift. It declares, “I am not God; the world keeps turning without me.” Being willing to stop is acknowledging that God is in control.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Refusing to rest is often the other face of self-rule—thinking everything depends on me. Rest is returning to our human place: let people be people and let God be God. As our perspective shifts from the temporary to the eternal, even our time becomes part of building what belongs to God.
q: Who is God? — God “blessed the seventh day”; what does this show you about his care for people?
Who am I? — Do you often feel that stopping is a waste—or even feel guilty about it?
How shall I respond? — At what time this week will you deliberately set your work aside?
lessons.jesus: Jesus regularly went to the synagogue on the Sabbath, and on the Sabbath he also healed the sick and set people free. He said, “My Father is still working, so I am working too.” He turned the Sabbath from a rule that binds people into a day when God restores people and makes them whole.
lessons.pray: Creator God, thank you for placing the gift of rest within time. I confess that I often treat busyness as my worth and refuse to stop. Teach me to remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy, and when I stop, to acknowledge that you are God. May my life follow your rhythm rather than being driven by anxiety. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set aside thirty minutes today with no work and no scrolling
Write down one piece of work you can let go of and hand over to God
Choose a full block of rest this week and write it in your calendar
lessons.noon: “God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy.” — Lord, right now I rest a while in you.

lessons.title: Taking the Lord’s Yoke
lessons.theme: Exchange your yoke for Jesus’ yoke, and your soul will find rest

v: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

lessons.still: Imagine you are carrying a heavy pack, filled with responsibilities, expectations and worries. In front of Jesus, take them out one by one and set them down. Then hear him say, “Take my yoke upon you and learn from me.” Receive the light burden he hands you.
teach: In ancient times a yoke was a wooden frame fitted across an ox’s shoulders. A good carpenter would shape each yoke to fit its ox, so that it sat well and didn’t chafe. Jesus worked as a carpenter in Nazareth, and when he says, “My yoke is easy,” the word also carries the sense of “well-fitting, good to use”—the burden he gives is made to measure.

Jesus’ invitation is not “You don’t have to carry anything,” but “Change your yoke.” The yoke we were carrying was our own: proving ourselves, pleasing people, controlling everything. Jesus says, “Take my yoke upon you and learn from me”—he is the one who shares the yoke with us and leads the way. The secret lies in “I am gentle and humble in heart”: rest comes from learning his humility.

Much of our weariness is not because there is too much to do, but because our pride is too heavy: needing to save face, needing to be perfect, needing others to do things my way. Taking up the Lord’s yoke means laying down these self-imposed burdens and sharing the yoke with him. The work is still there, but our souls find rest.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is laying down power and returning to our place—this is exactly Jesus’ yoke. The yoke of self-rule is as heavy as a millstone; the yoke of the self-emptied life is easy and light. Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself: share the yoke with the Lord, and living from the heart brings joy.
q: Who is God? — What does a Lord who says “Come to me” mean for you in your weariness?
Who am I? — What “yoke of your own” are you carrying on your shoulders that the Lord never asked you to carry?
How shall I respond? — Which aspect of Jesus’ “gentle and humble” way will you learn today?
lessons.jesus: Just before giving this invitation, Jesus had been rejected by many towns, yet he said, “Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.” His rest came from wholly accepting the Father’s will. He carried the heaviest cross of all, so that we could carry his light yoke.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I labour and am heavily burdened, often carrying yokes you never asked me to carry. Today I come to you and lay down the burden of proving myself and controlling everything. I am willing to take your yoke and learn your gentle and humble ways. Let my soul find rest even in the midst of my work. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one “yoke of your own,” and beside it write: “Given to the Lord”
As you do a task today, pray silently: “Lord, let’s do this together”
lessons.noon: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened.” — Lord, right now I come to you.

lessons.title: The Faith to Stop
lessons.theme: Stopping means trusting that God is more reliable than I am

v: Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.
There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.

lessons.still: Close your eyes and call to mind, one by one, the things you haven’t finished today. For each one, say, “Lord, you watch over this.” Then breathe in deeply and breathe out slowly, and let your body truly relax.
teach: A baby sleeps soundly in its mother’s arms—not because it has solved all its problems, but because it trusts the one holding it. Adults often sleep poorly, because we think that the moment we close our eyes, the world will spin out of control.

Psalm 127 says that unless the Lord builds and watches over, it is “vain” to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil; “for he gives sleep to his loved ones.” Sleep becomes an act of faith. Hebrews says that those who enter his rest have “rested from their works”—not that they no longer work, but that they no longer rely on their work to be saved or to have worth.

Stopping takes faith: trusting that God is still at work while I rest. The greatest temptation in our work is to think that success or failure rests entirely on us. Being willing to stop when it is time to stop is saying to God, “You are the builder; I am your co-worker.” Rest like this keeps us from being swallowed by busyness or crushed by failure.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Everything is what God has done and accomplished in Jesus; all of it is grace. Resting from our own works is the mark of a life of grace; refusing to stop because everything depends on me is the mark of self-rule. When we let Jesus reign, even our sleep becomes trust and worship.
q: Who is God? — “He gives sleep to his loved ones”: what does this show you about God’s love?
Who am I? — Do you feel that success or failure rests entirely on you?
How shall I respond? — Tonight, how will you express your trust by “sleeping in peace”?
lessons.jesus: A great storm arose on the Sea of Galilee and the boat was about to sink, yet Jesus was asleep in the stern. His sleep was not irresponsibility but complete trust in the Father. When his panicked disciples cried out, he got up, calmed the storm, and asked them why they were afraid. He invites us, too, to rest in the storm.
lessons.pray: Lord, unless you build the house, all my labour is in vain. I often think that if I stop, things will fall apart, so I sleep poorly at night. Today I hand my unfinished tasks to you to watch over, and I rest from my own works. Let me sleep in peace like a baby in its mother’s arms. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before bed, write down three things for tomorrow, then pray and entrust them to God
Set a time to stop work today, and when it comes, really stop
About one thing you cannot control, say: “Lord, you watch over this”
lessons.noon: “For he gives sleep to his loved ones.” — Lord, right now I place my burdens in your hands.

lessons.title: The Lord’s Day: Worship and Renewal
lessons.theme: The Lord’s Day is a day to be renewed together with God and his people

v: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

lessons.still: Think back to last Sunday: did you rush in late with your mind elsewhere, or did you come with a heart prepared to worship? Quietly tell the Lord, “Lord, this Lord’s Day I want to come before you with a prepared heart.”
teach: Phones need charging every day, and cars need regular servicing; otherwise even the best machine will break down halfway. The Lord’s Day is like regular servicing for the soul: meeting with God, gathering with brothers and sisters, resting body and mind, and then setting out again.

Jesus said, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.” Rest is not a burden but a gift; and he is “lord even of the Sabbath”—he himself is the centre of our rest. The early church gathered to break bread on the first day of the week, the day the Lord rose. Hebrews reminds us not to forsake meeting together, but to consider how to spur one another on to love and good works.

The Lord’s Day has two emphases: worship and rest. Worship refocuses the whole week on God; rest is trusting God’s provision. Don’t let the Lord’s Day become another busy workday, and don’t treat it merely as a holiday for sleeping till noon. It is a day to be renewed together with God and with his people.
lessons.light: 321 Light: First with God, then with people, then with tasks. Sunday worship is the day we realign the order of our relationships; caring for one another is the 235 life of walking with spiritual companions. Letting Jesus receive all the glory begins with Sunday worship and extends into every day of the week.
q: Who is God? — Jesus is “lord even of the Sabbath”; what does this mean for your Lord’s Day?
Who am I? — Is your Lord’s Day more like recharging and servicing, or just another kind of busyness?
How shall I respond? — This Lord’s Day, how will you prepare your heart to worship and also truly rest?
lessons.jesus: On the Sabbath Jesus went into the synagogue “as was his custom” and worshipped with the people. He rose on the first day of the week and appeared to his disciples and was with them. He is not only Lord of the Sabbath; he is the Lord who is with us when we gather.
lessons.pray: Lord of the Sabbath, thank you for giving me the Lord’s Day to service and renew my soul. Help me not to forsake meeting together, to come with a heart prepared to worship you, and to care for my brothers and sisters. May my Lord’s Day not be stolen by busyness, but be a day of rest and strength in you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Go to bed early the night before the Lord’s Day, and prepare your heart to worship
This Lord’s Day, reach out to someone at church who is often overlooked
Set aside time on the Lord’s Day to rest well with your family
lessons.noon: “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.” — Lord, right now I am renewed in you.

lessons.title: The Rhythm of Life
lessons.theme: Living by God’s rhythm makes for a spiritual life that lasts

v: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

lessons.still: Take out your calendar or phone and quietly look over this week’s schedule. Ask the Lord, “Which of these do you want me to do? Where do I need to stop?” Let the Holy Spirit point out one place that needs adjusting.
teach: The heart contracts and relaxes, never stopping for a lifetime, because it has a rhythm: every contraction is followed by relaxation. A heart that only contracted and never relaxed would fail. Spiritual life needs rhythm too: work and rest, service and retreat, community and solitude, taking their turns.

When the disciples came back from their preaching mission, they were so busy they didn’t even have time to eat. So Jesus said, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” The Lord not only sends people out to work; he personally leads them to rest. Moses prayed, “So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.” Rhythm means using wisely the days God gives us.

Over these seven weeks we have built the basic practices: coming home, stillness, Scripture, prayer, humility, victory and rest. Now we arrange them into a workable rhythm: daily stillness, Bible reading and prayer; the weekly Lord’s Day and Sabbath rest; and a quarterly retreat and review. Next week we will see the foundation beneath it all: the assurance of salvation.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and your life will change; change your life and the way you live will change. Rhythm means writing truth into the schedule of our lives. When we practise, review, correct and repeat regularly, our lives grow steadily, building what belongs to God step by step.
q: Who is God? — The Lord says, “Come… and rest awhile”; what does this show you about his considerate care?
Who am I? — Is your current rhythm of life more like a heart that contracts and relaxes, or one that only contracts and never relaxes?
How shall I respond? — What daily and weekly rhythm will you write down for yourself?
lessons.jesus: Jesus’ life had a clear rhythm: praying alone in the early morning, serving among the crowds by day, going to the synagogue on the Sabbath, and often taking his disciples away to quiet places. He was never driven by needs, but acted according to the Father’s timing. He is the model for the rhythm of our lives.
lessons.pray: Lord, teach me to count my days, that I may gain a heart of wisdom. My life often only contracts and never relaxes; I am so busy I don’t even have time to be with you. Help me to build a rhythm that belongs to you: drawing near to you every day, resting and worshipping every week, and often going away with you to rest awhile. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down your daily rhythm: what time you will be still, read Scripture and pray
Mark this week’s rest time and the Lord’s Day on your calendar
Share your rhythm of life with a spiritual companion and ask them to check in weekly
lessons.noon: “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” — Lord, right now I go with you to rest awhile.
